issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

 I am filing it because the minimized case shows an Inductor-only dtype contract violation on both the 2.13 release and the latest nightly.

>
> On CPU, `torch.compile(..., backend="inductor")` changes the output dtype of some same-dtype `int8` batched matrix multiplications from `torch.int8` to `torch.int64`. Native eager, the `eager` backend, and `aot_eager` all return `torch.int8`.
>
> The numerical values happen to match in this small example, but the output dtype does not. This can change downstream type promotion and dispatch.
>
> Minimal self-contained reproducer:
>
> ```python
> import torch
>
> def model(a, b):
>     return torch.matmul(a, b)
>
> a = torch.ones((1, 1, 2), dtype=torch.int8)
> b = torch.ones((1, 2, 2), dtype=torch.int8)
>
> eager = model(a, b)
> compiled = torch.compile(
>     model,
>     backend="inductor",
>     fullgraph=True,
>     dynamic=False,
> )(a, b)
>
> print("torch:", torch.__version__)
> print("git:", torch.version.git_version)
> print("eager:", eager, eager.dtype)
> print("compiled:", compiled, compiled.dtype)
>
> assert compiled.dtype == eager.dtype
> ```
>
> Output on the latest nightly:
>
> ```text
> torch: 2.14.0.dev20260727
> git: ee6a51f8364b126e4e3a3d4459f8fbb35d6a5d3a
> eager:    tensor([[[2, 2]]], dtype=torch.int8)  torch.int8
> compiled: tensor([[[2, 2]]])                    torch.int64
> AssertionError
> ```
>
> The same reproducer also fails on PyTorch `2.13.0`, git commit `cf30153c4c131c8164ee7798e5022d810682e2cb`.
>
> Backend/settings ablation on `2.14.0.dev20260727`:
>
> | Execution | `dynamic=False` | `dynamic=True` |
> |---|---|---|
> | native eager | `torch.int8` | `torch.int8` |
> | `backend="eager"` | `torch.int8` | `torch.int8` |
> | `backend="aot_eager"` | `torch.int8` | `torch.int8` |
> | `backend="inductor"` | **`torch.int64`** | **`torch.int64`** |
>
> `torch.bmm` shows the same behavior. Contiguous and non-contiguous inputs both reproduce it. Three additional independent processes with fresh `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` values reproduced it 3/3.
>
> Shape boundary observed during minimization:
>
> - Affected examples include `(1,1,2) @ (1,2,2)`, `(1,2,2) @ (1,2,1)`, and `(2,2,3) @ (2,3,1)`.
> - Tested 2-D `mm` shapes return the correct `torch.int8` dtype.
> - Some 3-D square or degenerate shapes also return the correct dtype, so rank 3 alone is not sufficient.
>
> This is an integer dtype comparison: no floating-point tolerance is involved, no max/min indices are compared, and the reproducer contains no randomness.
>
> I did not find an exact duplicate. The closest reports I found were #177629, #177630, and #172183, but those concern mixed floating dtypes where eager raises while compiled execution succeeds. #144362 is a broader dtype-check tracker.

My assessment is that this is a correctness issue even though the small example's values match, because compiled execution should preserve eager's output dtype and downstream behavior can depend on it. The quoted technical section above was prepared with Codex assistance; the experiment and decision to report the reproduced dtype violation are mine.

### Error logs

> No compiler exception is raised. The failure is the explicit dtype assertion:
>
> ```text
> eager dtype:    torch.int8
> compiled dtype: torch.int64
> AssertionError
> ```

### Versions

> ```text
> Collecting environment information...
> PyTorch version: 2.14.0.dev20260727
> Is debug build: False
> CUDA used to build PyTorch: None
> ROCM used to build PyTorch: N/A
>
> OS: macOS 26.0 (arm64)
> GCC version: Could not collect
> Clang version: 17.0.0 (clang-1700.0.13.5)
> CMake version: Could not collect
> Libc version: N/A
>
> Python version: 3.12.10 | packaged by conda-forge | (main, Apr 10 2025, 22:19:24) [Clang 18.1.8 ] (64-bit runtime)
> Python platform: macOS-26.0-arm64-arm-64bit
> Is CUDA available: False
> CUDA runtime version: No CUDA
> CUDA_MODULE_LOADING set to: N/A
> GPU models and configuration: No CUDA
> Nvidia driver version: No CUDA
> cuDNN version: No CUDA
> Is XPU available: False
> HIP runtime version: N/A
> MIOpen runtime version: N/A
> Is XNNPACK available: False
> Caching allocator config: N/A
>
> CPU:
> Apple M1 Pro
>
> Versions of relevant libraries:
> [pip3] torch==2.14.0.dev20260727
> ```

issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #191308. On CPU, `torch.compile(backend="inductor")` changed the output dtype of same-dtype integer `bmm`/`matmul` from the input dtype (e.g. `int8`) to `int64`, while eager, `eager` backend, and `aot_eager` all preserve the input dtype.

The CPU-specific decomposition in `tuned_bmm` (taken when `mat1` has M==1 or `mat2` has N==1) lowers bmm to a broadcasted mul followed by a sum. For integer inputs the reduction accumulates at the compute type (`int64`), and the result was returned as-is, leaking the accumulator dtype into the output. The reduction result is now cast back to the input dtype. For float inputs the cast is a no-op, and the int64 accumulator already matches or exceeds eager's accumulation precision, so values are unchanged.

The dot-shaped CUDA/XPU decomposition above it is restricted to float dtypes and unaffected.

## Test plan

- New regression test `test_bmm_cpu_decompose_preserves_integer_output_dtype` in `test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py`: bmm with M==1 across int8/int32/int64/float32 asserts compiled dtype equals eager dtype and values match.
- Verified on this machine (arm64 macOS, torch 2.13.0) by patching the installed wheel's `torch/_inductor/kernel/bmm.py` in place and running the issue repro plus the four-dtype matrix: before, `compiled.dtype == torch.int64` vs eager `int8`; after, all four dtypes match eager and `(compiled == eager).all()` holds. The in-tree test file imports symbols newer than the 2.13.0 wheel, so it was validated by its standalone equivalent rather than run from the test module itself; a full source build was not run on macOS.

issue.body:
# FINDINGS

Ground truth for the five regression-corpus cases in `cases/`. Filled only
from runs actually executed for slice C-1 (see the PR's Evidence Report for
full command/output transcripts).

**Canonical verification run:** `/tmp/baumeister_clean_venv`, a venv created
fresh for this purpose (`pip install --index-url
https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cpu torch`, nothing else on top),
Python 3.10.12, torch `2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu`, git
`279f79e09c3f3ef458061013bda2d2f483c02cae`, aarch64 Linux, CPU-only,
`TORCHINDUCTOR_FORCE_DISABLE_CACHES=1`. This matches the CEO's independent
ashburn run bit for bit. No other architecture or accelerator was run.

**Environment-integrity note, resolved: the "contamination" was our own
fix-in-progress for 195451, not a rogue patch.** An earlier pass verified
against a pre-existing `/tmp/pruefer_venv` (torch `2.15.0.dev20260831+cpu`)
and got a GREEN on `alias_slice_scatter_copyback.py` where every unpatched
nightly checked (0824, 0831, 0901) is RED. That venv's
`torch/_inductor/fx_passes/reinplace.py` has a hand-applied
`should_reinplace_scatter()` escape-check guard (function
`_scatter_result_escapes_graph`) -- confirmed absent from official
pytorch/pytorch source at the exact commit that venv's own
`torch.version.git_version` reports, and absent from current
pytorch/pytorch main (`gh api search/code` found zero matches), by diffing
the installed file against `gh api
repos/pytorch/pytorch/contents/...?ref=<commit>`. This is the same bug, the
same author, and the same day as the open fix
[PR #195484](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/195484) -- but it is
NOT textually identical to that PR's current diff (different function name,
different control-flow placement inside `should_reinplace_scatter`,
recursive vs. iterative traversal); most likely an earlier local iteration
of the same fix, applied directly to that venv's site-packages rather than
landed as a commit. So the GREEN was real: reinplacing genuinely does not
fire with that guard in the tree. It reflects "the fix, in some form, is
present" rather than "the bug is absent upstream." Every other file spot-
checked in that venv -- the files touched by the fixes behind the other
four cases -- matched official source exactly; only this one file carried a
local patch. All five cases below were re-run in a clean venv (guard not
present) to get the upstream-accurate baseline; only case 1's result
changed there (GREEN to RED, matching every unpatched nightly). Verification
venvs should be created fresh per mission and removed after -- a patched
venv should not outlive the mission that patched it.

| Case | Issue | PR | Status upstream | Oracle | First diverging backend | RED on (torch versions run) | GREEN on (torch versions run) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alias_slice_scatter_copyback.py` | [#195451](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/195451) | [#195484](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/195484) (open, unmerged; an earlier local iteration of this fix is what caused the GREEN discussed in the note above) | open, unmerged upstream | alias | not established (only `inductor` run; `--backend aot_eager` available but not separately confirmed against this build) | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (clean venv, default `inductor`), plus 0824 and 0831 nightlies per the CEO's and Baumeister's cross-checks | not run on any unpatched build; GREEN only observed with the local fix-iteration guard in the tree (see note) |
| `alias_noop_view_identity.py` | [#191449](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191449) | [#191844](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/191844) (merged 2026-09-02T03:45:57Z, commit `a3586f0018`) | merged 2026-09-02 | alias | `inductor` (fix location: AOTAutograd -- see note below on why those differ) | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (clean venv, default `inductor`) -- this build predates the 03:45 UTC merge | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (`--backend aot_eager` only) |
| `dtype_int8_matmul_promotion.py` | [#191308](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191308) | none found | open, unfixed | metadata (dtype) | `inductor` | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (clean venv, default `inductor`) | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (`--backend aot_eager`) |
| `distributions_validation_branch.py` | [#194593](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194593) (sibling [#194596](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194596)) | none found | open, unfixed | graph (fullgraph capturability) | not established (both `inductor` and `aot_eager` raised under `fullgraph=True`) | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (clean venv, `fullgraph=True`, `inductor` and `--backend aot_eager`) | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (default `fullgraph=False` mode, context probe only, not a separate case file) |
| `numerics_cpu_inductor_miscompile.py` | [#190765](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/190765) | [#190966](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/190966) ("Fixes #190765"; `ModularIndexing` negativity guard) | fixed by #190966 | numerics | not run (matched eager; no divergence observed) | expected on torch <= 2.13.x (pre-fix; not independently re-run here) | 2.15.0.dev20260901+cpu, aarch64, CPU (clean venv, default `inductor`, and `--backend aot_eager`) -- confirmed the guard is present in this build's `torch/utils/_sympy/functions.py`, diffed against official source at the same commit: match |

## Notes on surprises (not predicted by the slice brief)

- **195451 IS RED, as the brief expected, on every unpatched nightly
  checked (0824, 0831, 0901).** The earlier GREEN pass wasn't a false
  negative against an absent bug -- it was a true positive against a
  present, not-yet-landed fix: an earlier local iteration of PR 195484 had
  been applied directly to that venv's `reinplace.py`. See the
  environment-integrity note above. PR 195484 itself is still open,
  unmerged upstream.
- **191449: first diverging backend is `inductor`, fix location is
  AOTAutograd -- confirmed, and these are two different things, not a
  contradiction.** Re-run on the 0901 nightly: both MWEs (resize-on-view and
  the two-object identity check) are RED under `inductor`, GREEN under
  `aot_eager`. The fix (PR 191844) lives entirely in AOTAutograd's
  `run_functionalized_fw_and_collect_metadata` -- backend-independent code
  -- yet the symptom is only observable when the backend actually hands
  back one buffer object for two logical outputs; `aot_eager`'s eager
  kernels return distinct view objects regardless of AOTAutograd's
  (mis)classification, so the bug never surfaces there even pre-fix. A
  stage verdict (which backend diverges) says where the divergence becomes
  *visible*, never where the bug *lives* -- the general form of this rule is
  now in PLAN.md's stage-localization section.
- **190765 GREEN is expected, not a surprise.** Fixed upstream by
  [PR #190966](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/190966) ("Fixes
  #190765"): a negativity guard on `ModularIndexing`'s term-stripping in
  Inductor's sympy simplification, so the strip is only applied when every
  surviving term is provably nonnegative. Confirmed present in the clean
  venv's `torch/utils/_sympy/functions.py`, and that file was diffed byte-
  for-byte against the official pytorch/pytorch source at the same commit
  (match) -- unlike case 1, this fix is genuinely upstream, not a local
  patch. RED expected on any torch build that predates it (e.g. 2.13.x, per
  the issue's own environment); GREEN expected on any build that contains
  it.
- **194593's contract violation is a `fullgraph=True` graph break
  ("Data-dependent branching", gb0170)**, not literally a `_validate_args`
  divergence as the slice brief speculated. Root cause and the branch line
  (`_kl_binomial_binomial`'s `if (p.total_count < q.total_count).any():`)
  were confirmed directly against the issue text.

AI assisted.

issue.body:
Corpus integration for M2: the corpus now knows which torch it is supposed to
fail on, CI says so on the job page, and every case goes through the oracles in
one test instead of four hand-written ones. Plus the two pieces of housekeeping
the M2-2 verification asked for.

## The version markers

PLAN.md "Regression corpus" asks for a known-bad version marker per case,
because several of these bugs are already fixed and a case cannot simply assert
"this fails": [#190765](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/190765) is
GREEN from 2.14 on, [#191449](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191449)
turned GREEN mid-nightly when `a3586f00181` landed on 2026-09-02, and
[#195451](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/195451),
[#191308](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191308) and
[#194593](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194593) are open.

`cases/markers.py` is that table as data, and
`expected_verdict(case, torch_version, git_version)` is the one place the
version arithmetic happens:

- a **release** compares by version number;
- a **nightly** compares by its date, because a fix that lands mid-cycle splits
  one release line in two (`2.15.0.dev20260901` is RED for 191449 and
  `2.15.0.dev20260902` is GREEN);
- the **build commit** is read first where it is known, since a hash is exact
  where a version string is an inference — it is also the only handle on a
  `2.15.0a0+gitdeadbeef` that cannot be placed otherwise;
- a build that cannot be placed against a known fix comes back `UNKNOWN`, never
  a guess.

Each `CaseMarker` field is a fact with a provenance, which is why there are
several: `known_bad` is "we measured RED on this build", `fixed_in_release` is
"the fix landed, so anything later must be GREEN". A table that flattened the
two would let an inference go stale unnoticed. Nothing in the module imports
torch, so the arithmetic is tested against version strings rather than against
whatever this machine happens to have installed.

## What checks it

`tests/test_corpus_markers.py` runs each standalone script and compares its live
verdict with the marker. **A disagreement is a warning, not a failure.** Turning
it into a red build would mean a nightly that fixes a bug upstream breaks this
repository, which is the exact failure mode the marker exists to avoid. Every
case also prints one grep-able line:

```
CORPUS alias_slice_scatter_copyback observed=RED expected=RED torch=2.14.0+cpu
CORPUS alias_noop_view_identity observed=RED expected=RED torch=2.14.0+cpu
CORPUS dtype_int8_matmul_promotion observed=RED expected=RED torch=2.14.0+cpu
CORPUS distributions_validation_branch observed=RED expected=RED torch=2.14.0+cpu
CORPUS numerics_cpu_inductor_miscompile observed=GREEN expected=GREEN torch=2.14.0+cpu
```

## The CI job summary

`cases/summary.py` runs every case and renders the same information as a table;
a step after pytest appends it to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` on every matrix cell,
`if: always()` — the table is most wanted on the cell that just went red, since
it is how you tell "torch changed" from "the tool broke". The module prints to
stdout and knows nothing about GitHub, so it stays runnable and testable
anywhere; the redirect is the one line of workflow.

`python -m cases.summary`, on this box:

### compile-check regression corpus -- torch 2.14.0+cpu (git 08187d9e0fba), python 3.10.12, aarch64

| Case | Issue | Oracle | Observed | Expected | Agrees |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alias_slice_scatter_copyback` | [#195451](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/195451) | alias | RED | RED | yes |
| `alias_noop_view_identity` | [#191449](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191449) | alias | RED | RED | yes |
| `dtype_int8_matmul_promotion` | [#191308](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191308) | metadata | RED | RED | yes |
| `distributions_validation_branch` | [#194593](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194593) | graph | RED | RED | yes |
| `numerics_cpu_inductor_miscompile` | [#190765](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/190765) | numerics | GREEN | GREEN | yes |

5 cases: 5 agree with the marker, 0 disagree, 0 could not be placed.

## The corpus through the oracles, once

M2-1 and M2-2 grew a fixture and a test per case, four of them, each repeating
the same six lines of setup — and between them they covered three of the five
cases. `tests/test_corpus_oracles.py` is the parametrized version: import the
case, `build()`, run it through the runner and every oracle, and grade the
findings against the case's own `check()`. RED means at least one fail finding
from the oracle that case belongs to, GREEN means none, and the stage verdict
must name the first lane that broke.

Three things the table has to carry, because the corpus is not uniform and
pretending it was would have been the easy wrong answer:

- **each `check()` reads a different shape** — a value, a live `(input, output)`
  pair, a `(raised, payload)` attempt, a list of repeated outputs — so the
  adapter is per case and says what it is adapting;
- **the oracle a RED reaches the report through** is the one for the shape
  `build()` returns, which for 191449 is numerics + metadata rather than alias:
  that `build()` resizes through the collapsed view and returns a *value*. The
  alias-oracle view of the same bug keeps its own test, now driven by the twin
  `cases/alias_noop_view.py`, which is exactly that shape;
- **194593's RED is a lane that raises** under `fullgraph=True`, which is exit 1
  by the raised-lane rule and belongs to no oracle category at all.

`check()` is asked *after* every oracle has run, because 195451's RED probe
writes into the compiled output to prove the alias is load-bearing, and an
oracle reading that tensor afterwards would be reading the probe.

The flags each case needs and the backend its verdict lands on come from
`tests/test_corpus_twins.py`'s own table, so the two modules cannot disagree,
and a third test asserts the three tables that describe the corpus — `CORPUS`,
`TWINS`, `MARKERS` — still list the same cases. What is deliberately not
repeated is the twins module's assertions: it grades the CLI's exit code and
stage line, this one grades which oracle fired.

`tests/test_oracles.py` keeps the version-independent halves — each bug as a
synthetic result, which pins the oracle's rule down on a torch where the bug is
long fixed.

## Housekeeping (a): `--seed` reaches a model built at import time

The seed was applied per lane inside the runner, which is what makes the lanes
comparable, and nowhere before that, which is what makes two *runs* comparable.
A target that builds its model at module scope — the shape
`model = torchvision.models.resnet18(weights=None)` has — draws its weights
while `load_target` is executing the module, so `--seed` never reached them.
The CLI now seeds before discovery as well.

Two runs of `compile-check validation/targets/tv_resnet18.py --backends eager
--seed N`, hashing what the target computes afterwards:

```
seed 0  DIGEST 4012463f322ce3880813ba26100e64c67551648a487f29967be713a975b79940
seed 0  DIGEST 4012463f322ce3880813ba26100e64c67551648a487f29967be713a975b79940
seed 1  DIGEST ba42e6ce81a9c5de1ee173a2bc867e3505995493f0efa4aa527545f359524a82
```

Both assertions matter: same seed twice must agree, which is what was broken,
and a different seed must not, which is what says the determinism comes from the
seed rather than from torch starting in a fixed state.
`tests/fixtures/random_at_import.py` is the fixture that shape is tested with.

## Housekeeping (b): `--grad-tol-factor`

The grad oracle compared gradients at the *output* tolerances, and the M2-2
verifier watched a compiled resnet18 gradient sit about 1.24e-5 from eager's
against a float32 atol of 1e-5 — the same run came back clean or failing
depending on the last bit. `--grad-tol-factor` (default 10) multiplies the
numerics tolerances for gradient **values** only; the output tolerances are
untouched, because the reason for the looser rule is how a backward accumulates
and lending it to the forward comparison would blunt the oracle that catches
190765. The report's environment block records the factor a clean grad row was
reached under:

```
  gradients compared at the numerics tolerances x10 (--grad-tol-factor 10)
  gradients compared at the numerics tolerances (--grad-tol-factor 1)
  gradients not compared (--no-grad)
```

Ten clears the borderline case and not every model, and that is recorded where
the constant lives rather than assumed. Measured here on torchvision resnet18 at
`2x3x64x64`, torch 2.14.0+cpu, aarch64, seed 0 — the factor inductor needs
before every gradient passes:

| mode | aot_eager | inductor | past 1x | past 10x |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model.eval()` | bit-identical | 1.0x (worst gradient 1.34e-5 vs atol 1e-5) | 0/63 | 0/63 |
| `model.train()` | bit-identical | ~161x | 61/63 | 21/63 |

Batch norm is the whole difference: in train mode every gradient travels back
through a mean and a variance computed from the batch. It is not a miscompile —
against a float64 eager reference the two lanes sit at the same order of error
in the train-mode row (worst per-tensor `max|diff|/max|ref|`: 3.4e-5 for eager,
3.9e-5 for inductor), which is PLAN.md "The oracle blind spot"'s *both
imprecise* rather than *compiled is wrong*. No single constant is right for both
a two-layer MLP (bit-identical, needs 1x) and a resnet, so the default clears the
measured borderline case, the flag is how a real model is run, and per-op
tolerances are the documented next step rather than a bigger constant.

One commit here corrects that record: it was filed against "this repo's own
validation target", which is eval mode at batch 1, where the same measurement
comes back 1.0x.

## Verification

Repo-root gate, torch 2.14.0+cpu (git `08187d9e0fba`), python 3.10.12, aarch64,
CPU-only, caches disabled:

```
$ ruff check .
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check .
75 files already formatted
$ mypy src/
Success: no issues found in 20 source files
$ pytest -q
265 passed, 1 skipped, 55 warnings in 132.84s
```

The one skip is `numerics_cpu_inductor_miscompile`: 190765 is fixed on this
torch, so its case is GREEN and there is no finding to assert.

Every file in `cases/` run standalone:

```
cases/alias_copyback.py                    exit=0
cases/alias_noop_view.py                   exit=0
cases/alias_noop_view_identity.py          exit=1  RED  ... compiled output diverges from eager after resize_() on a no-op view
cases/alias_slice_scatter_copyback.py      exit=1  RED  ... mutating the output corrupted the input: before=[10.0, 2.0] after=[110.0, 102.0]
cases/distributions_binomial_kl.py         exit=0
cases/distributions_validation_branch.py   exit=1  RED  ... fullgraph=True raised where eager succeeded: Unsupported: Data-dependent branching
cases/dtype_int8_matmul_promotion.py       exit=1  RED  ... compiled dtype torch.int64 != eager dtype torch.int8
cases/dtype_promotion.py                   exit=0
cases/markers.py                           exit=0
cases/numerics_cpu_inductor_miscompile.py  exit=0  GREEN ... matched eager and was deterministic across 4 runs
cases/numerics_polyjuice_minmax.py         exit=0
cases/summary.py                           exit=0  (the table)
```

`cases/summary.py` was the one file in that directory that could not be run
directly — `python cases/summary.py` puts `cases/` on the path rather than the
root, so `cases.markers` did not resolve. Four guarded lines fix it; `-m` is
unaffected and is still what CI runs.

`compile-check cases/alias_copyback.py` — 195451 through the tool, exit 1:

```
checks
  oracle    fail-on  aot_eager         inductor
  numerics  yes      pass              pass
  alias     yes      pass              1 fail
  metadata  yes      pass              pass
  grad      yes      pass              pass
  graph     no       not yet           not yet

findings
  alias  (1 fail)
    [fail] inductor output[0]
        inductor returned input[0] itself as output[0] and eager returned a distinct object
        field identity_added   expected output[0]~input[0] unrelated   got output[0]~input[0] same
        object/overlapping

stage
  first diverges at inductor, which implicates inductor lowering/codegen
  that is where the divergence becomes observable, not necessarily where the fix belongs
```

issue.body:
Closes the first half of M3's report work: PLAN.md "Reports" asks for three
outputs behind one model, and the terminal report was the only one that
existed. `--json`, `--md` and `--emit-test` now write the other three
artifacts off a single run.

## What landed

**`report/json.py` — the CI-consumable artifact.** `schema_version` 1,
documented in the module docstring and enforced by a hand-rolled
`validate()` (no new dependency: PLAN.md keeps torch the only runtime
requirement). It carries the environment block with the architecture always
in it, the run configuration — including the module handling that *actually
happened*, so a run whose lanes shared one object because the deep copy
failed says so in the artifact as well as on the terminal — one record per
lane with its timings, its exception, its repeat-call exception and its
graph health, every finding with its details, the verdict with the per-lane
counts behind it, and the exit code. `dump()` refuses to write a document
that fails validation: a report that does not match its own schema is a bug
in the tool, and writing it anyway would hand a CI job an artifact its
consumer cannot read.

Two absences are deliberate. There is no timestamp — PLAN.md
"Cross-architecture parity is a feature" makes parity in v1 "run the tool on
two machines and diff the two JSON files", and a field that differs on every
run for no reason makes that diff worse. And there is no `compile-check
compare a.json b.json`; that subcommand is v0.2, and the module says so.

**`report/markdown.py` — the issue draft.** The shape the PyTorch tracker
expects: a title naming the lane and what changed, the repro inline as a
fenced block, expected versus got per finding, the stage line with PLAN.md's
observability caveat, the emitted regression test, the environment block
(torch version and git hash, python, OS, architecture and CPU flags, device,
backend configuration, module handling, cache mode), and the command that
produced it. It adds **no** disclosure line: whether and how a person
discloses tooling on an issue they file under their own name is theirs to
decide, and a tool that wrote it into the draft would be deciding it for
them.

**`report/pytest_case.py` — the regression test.** The top fail-severity
finding as a test method in the idiom `test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py`
uses, with the assertion the oracle actually failed on: `assertEqual` on the
field for metadata, `assertIsNot` plus a `data_ptr` check for alias, a
backward per lane for grad, `explain` for graph, and
`torch.testing.assert_close` as the general form. A parameter gradient runs
the two lanes one after the other with the grads cleared between, because
`torch.compile(model)` wraps the module rather than copying it and both
backwards would otherwise accumulate into one `.grad`. Only a `fail` earns a
test — a contiguous-to-contiguous stride change is a legitimate layout
choice and the fp64 distance is context — so a clean run writes no file and
says which of the two reasons it was.

**`report/repro.py` — the shared reduction.** The draft and the emitter both
need one answer to "which lines of this file are the reproducer", so it is
derived once: the file is parsed and the closure of the entry point and the
inputs is kept. It is not the minimizer (M3-3 shrinks the run by re-running
it; nothing here runs anything), and a file whose entry point is bound
inside a `with` falls back to the whole file and says so rather than
guessing.

Supporting changes: `results.TargetSource` records where the target came
from so a report can quote it; `RunSet.module_handling` moves the
module-handling sentence onto the run so the terminal block and the JSON
block cannot drift apart; the alias oracle names its pair (`left`, `right`)
in the finding details so the emitter does not have to parse an English
sentence, and the terminal detail line skips them because the message
already says it.

Also in here, per the M3-1 verifier: README's status block and its note on
the action's pre-M1-3 behaviour were stale since PR #6, and are rewritten to
the current truth.

## The three artifacts, on the 191308 corpus twin

```console
$ compile-check cases/dtype_promotion.py --json out.json --md draft.md --emit-test test_case.py
compile-check: wrote out.json (--json)
compile-check: wrote draft.md (--md)
compile-check: wrote test_case.py (--emit-test)
```

`test_case.py` is the point of the slice — it reproduces
[191308](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191308) on torch 2.14 as
written:

```python
class TestDtypePromotion(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_dtype_promotion_fn_metadata_inductor(self):
        # https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191308
        expected = fn(*make_inputs())
        actual = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor")(*make_inputs())
        # dtype differs: eager torch.int8, inductor torch.int64
        self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, expected.dtype)
```

```console
$ pytest -q test_case.py
>       self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, expected.dtype)
E       AssertionError: torch.int64 != torch.int8
1 failed, 1 warning in 7.29s
```

On `cases/alias_copyback.py` the same path emits the 195451 shape instead:

```python
        eager_inputs = make_inputs()
        compiled_inputs = make_inputs()
        expected = fn(*eager_inputs)
        actual = torch.compile(fn, backend="inductor")(*compiled_inputs)
        # inductor returned input[0] itself as output[0] and eager returned a distinct object
        self.assertIsNot(actual, compiled_inputs[0])
        self.assertNotEqual(actual.data_ptr(), compiled_inputs[0].data_ptr())
```

And a clean run writes nothing rather than a test that asserts nothing:

```console
$ compile-check tests/fixtures/mlp.py --emit-test test_case.py
compile-check: --emit-test wrote no file: this run has no fail-severity finding and no
compiled lane that raised, so there is nothing for a regression test to assert
```

## Verification

Repository root, torch 2.14.0+cpu on aarch64, python 3.10.12:

```console
$ ruff check . && ruff format --check .
All checks passed!
81 files already formatted

$ mypy src/
Success: no issues found in 21 source files

$ pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider
414 passed, 1 skipped, 110 warnings in 151.50s

$ python -m cases.summary
5 cases: 5 agree with the marker, 0 disagree, 0 could not be placed.

$ python validation/run.py
tv_resnet18: clean
tv_mobilenet_v3_small: clean
tv_efficientnet_b0: clean
tv_vit_b_16_tiny: clean
hf_tiny_bert: skipped (transformers not installed (validation-only extra))
train_step_mlp: clean
```

The suite was run once more with `--basetemp=/tmp/pytest-of-runner/pytest-0`
so the temp paths match the GitHub runner's exactly, after the PR #13 red
where a report wrapped a path at a hyphen and passed locally on every cell
it failed in CI.

The suite goes from 326 tests to 414. 83 of the new ones are in
`tests/test_json_report.py` (27), `tests/test_pytest_case.py` (28),
`tests/test_markdown_report.py` (15) and `tests/test_repro.py` (13), and the
rest are the end-to-end artifact tests in `tests/test_cli.py`: the JSON
validates on a real run and survives a strict `json.load` round trip, the
Markdown draft is pinned as a snapshot, every oracle's assertion mapping is
checked, and every emitted file is `compile()`d with its imports asserted to
be torch and the standard library only.

AI assisted.

issue.body:
## What changed

Rewrites `README.md` in second-person, user-facing voice, and makes two
small supporting edits: moves an internals note into `docs/usage.md`, and
adds a `CHANGELOG.md` entry.

## Every factual claim changed or added, with evidence

**Process/milestone narration deleted.** The asciinema/`agg` detour, "this
repository has been public since 2026-09-03", "landed in M1-3", "destined
for the README", "not an accident of where this project happens to be
developed", and the CHANGELOG cross-reference calling a release a "slice"
are all removed or reworded without milestone jargon. Verified by
`grep -nE "this slice|landed in M|destined for|public since|agg|not an
accident" README.md` returning nothing.

**Regression corpus table.** Kept the five existing rows unchanged, added
one line under the table: "Every bug in this table was found and filed by
hand before this tool existed; the tool re-detects each one. Bugs first
found by torch-compile-check rather than by hand: none yet." Verified
every row's issue and PR state with `gh api repos/pytorch/pytorch/issues/N`
and `.../pulls/N`:

- [#195451](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/195451): open. [PR
  #195484](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/195484): open,
  `merged: false`. Matches "open, unmerged".
- [#191449](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191449): open. [PR
  #191844](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/191844): `state:
  closed`, `closed_at: 2026-09-02T03:46:03Z`, labeled `Merged` by
  pytorchbot (PyTorch lands via a bot push to `main`, not GitHub's native
  merge, so the REST `merged` boolean stays `false` even for a landed PR;
  the `Merged` label is the project's own ground truth). Matches "merged
  2026-09-02".
- [#191308](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/191308): open, no
  linked PR found. Matches "open, unfixed".
- [#194593](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194593) and
  [#194596](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/194596): both open.
  Matches "open, unfixed".
- [#190765](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/190765): closed. [PR
  #190966](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/190966): closed,
  labeled `Merged`. Matches "fixed, merged".
- The three "predate this tool" PRs ([#190673](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/190673),
  [#192628](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/192628)) and the
  excluded eager-autograd fix ([#192667](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/192667))
  are all closed and labeled `Merged`; #192667 carries `module: autograd`
  and `module: linear algebra`, consistent with "eager-autograd fix".

**Prior-art table gains a `torch.library.opcheck` row.** Verified by
importing it in the project's own venv:
`python -c "import torch.library; print(torch.library.opcheck)"` succeeds.
`torch.testing._internal.optests.operator_compile_check` does **not**
exist on this torch (`2.14.0+cpu`); the import raises `ImportError`. I
read `torch/testing/_internal/optests/generate_tests.py` in site-packages
instead of guessing: `opcheck()` runs exactly the entries in
`ALL_TEST_UTILS` — `test_schema`, `test_autograd_registration`,
`test_faketensor` (a `CrossRefFakeMode` check), `test_aot_dispatch_static`,
`test_aot_dispatch_dynamic` (both backed by `aot_autograd_check`, which
uses AOTAutograd's own `compiled_function`/`nop`, not inductor). There is
no inductor-lowering test anywhere in `opcheck`. The README row says so
explicitly ("does not exercise inductor lowering") rather than repeating
the original brief's assumption that it does; the original "make_fx"
description was also inaccurate (the fake-tensor check uses
`CrossRefFakeMode`, not `make_fx` tracing) so that word was dropped too.

**Static-shapes note**, per the CEO's second-pass refinement, added to
"Blind spot, stated up front": "v0.1 runs static shapes only
(`dynamic=False`, recorded in the JSON as `run.dynamic`); a dynamic-shapes
lane is planned." `dynamic: bool = False` is the literal default on
`run_all()` and `run_backend()` in `src/torch_compile_check/runner.py`,
and `report/json.py` writes it straight through as `run.dynamic`. The
"planned" half is PLAN.md's own v0.2 outlook line, "a dynamic shapes
matrix rather than a single optional pass" (today's `--dynamic` flag is
that single optional pass, not a shape matrix).

**Validation caption.** Table numbers are untouched, copied verbatim from
`docs/validation.md`. Added: "The same six targets also ran clean on
x86_64 CPU and on x86_64 with CUDA sm_75, 18 of 18 parity checks against
this aarch64 reference", pointing at `docs/cross-arch.md`'s
"Cross-architecture results (2026-09-03)" section, which records 6/6 (x86
CPU, ProBook leg) + 6/6 (x86 CPU, Omen leg) + 6/6 (x86+CUDA sm_75, Omen
leg) = 18/18 parity holds.

**Badges.** Added CI and Action self-test badges plus the existing MIT
badge. Every badge image URL and every link target verified `200` with
`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'`:
`.../actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg`,
`.../actions/workflows/ci.yml`,
`.../actions/workflows/action-selftest.yml/badge.svg`,
`.../actions/workflows/action-selftest.yml`.

**Action reference kept at `@main`**, not `@v0.1.0` (the tag does not
exist yet; `docs/release.md` step 8 is what flips it later).

**Moved verbatim**: the "What pointing the tool at a file does to your
interpreter" section moves into `docs/usage.md` (new `##` section right
after "Discovery overrides"), with a one-line pointer left in the README.

**Red-run transcript**: unchanged, re-verified by running
`torch-compile-check cases/dtype_promotion.py` fresh; output is
byte-identical to what was already in the README.

## Verification

- `ruff check .` — All checks passed!
- `ruff format --check .` — 93 files already formatted
- `mypy src/` — Success: no issues found in 21 source files
- `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` (full suite) — 569 passed, 1 skipped
  (pre-existing, unrelated torch-version skip), 193.32s
- Every relative link in `README.md` and `docs/usage.md` resolved with
  `test -e` (25/25)
- Every `http(s)` link (18) returned `200`
- `grep -n "—" README.md` — no output
- `grep -nE "this slice|landed in M|destined for|public since|agg|not an
  accident" README.md` — no output
- `tail -1 README.md` — `AI assisted.`

## Scope

`FINDINGS.md` and `PLAN.md` were not touched. Only `README.md`,
`docs/usage.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` changed.

AI assisted.
